goalbuddy_receipt_v1.rationale: T014 closes every T013 blocker. Working state now replays from separate append-only AEAD journals with sequence and previous-frame hashes; the encrypted manifest is only a snapshot. Pins and tombstones remain authoritative after manifest loss, injected post-fsync crashes, and rebuild. Reads, mutations, forks, and rebuilds require full workspace/project/session/set/evidence binding and validate canonical capture envelopes. Selection is recomputed deterministically, sibling forks use persisted UUIDv7 identities, and interim monolithic state fails closed. Capture acknowledges Working durability only after payload, journals, episode, and scoped reopen verification; degraded paths remain fail-open and offload cannot replace output. Fresh critical tests pass 45/45, Codex verification passes, and T014 reports all broad gates green.

worker_package.objective: Implement the blueprint’s bounded Lot 3 temporal knowledge-graph vertical slice without ontology learning, improve workers, router/MCP integration, deployment, or live infrastructure. Add immutable core ontology v1 containing only the approved entity and relation type allowlists and shape validators; do not support learned extensions, rename, merge, delete, shadow promotion, or ontology migration. Implement `knowledge-graph-adapter.mjs` with encrypted canonical vault records for entities, claims, temporal relations, projection checkpoints, and tombstones. Every recallable entity/claim/relation must be workspace-scoped, cite existing canonical episode and evidence IDs, carry a currently valid deterministic admission attestation, and preserve observed time plus `valid_from`/`valid_to`. Idempotent mutations must close superseded or contradicted relations without erasing history; episode tombstone or admission revocation must remove recall authority before projection cleanup and transitively requalify every dependent object. Provide a deterministic in-memory GraphEngine used by all local tests. Define the authenticated Graphiti+Neo4j remote projection contract and an injected direct-Neo4j fallback boundary; neither backend may decide truth, authorization, admission, or ontology, and backend loss must rebuild from encrypted vault records with equivalent hashes. Accept only a typed allowlisted query AST with workspace, starting entities, relation types, direction, `as_of`, and `max_hops`; default to 3 hops, reject above 5, reject raw Cypher and unknown fields before any backend call, and compile only parameterized backend requests. Revalidate backend results against canonical scope, admission, provenance, tombstones, and temporal validity before returning cited paths. Prove KG-AC01–09 and KG-AC12 using deterministic fixtures covering aliases explicitly bound to one entity, incompatible homonyms, contradiction/supersede history, `as_of`, cited three-hop paths, six-hop/raw-Cypher rejection, backend loss/rebuild, episode tombstone, admission revocation, cross-workspace indistinguishability, Graphiti failure with direct-Neo4j fallback, idempotence, encryption, and projection failure recovery. Tests must perform no network access and require no Graphiti, Neo4j, Hindsight, Ollama, credentials, container, or real vault.
stop_if: Any required implementation would overwrite, discard, or silently replace existing dirty user work instead of merging around it.
Any recallable graph object could exist without exact workspace scope, canonical episode and evidence provenance, and a valid active admission attestation.
Graphiti, Neo4j, the deterministic backend, or their returned IDs could become canonical or decide authorization, admission, truth, ontology, tombstone, revocation, or temporal validity.
A model/client-provided raw Cypher string, unknown AST field, non-allowlisted entity/relation type, invalid direction, or query above five hops could reach a backend.
Queries cannot enforce default three-hop and maximum five-hop bounds before backend execution, or foreign identifiers produce distinguishable existence signals.
A contradiction or supersede would overwrite historical evidence instead of closing `valid_to`, or an `as_of` query could return a relation outside its validity interval.
Episode tombstone or admission revocation cannot remove canonical recall authority before best-effort projection cleanup, or rebuild could resurrect revoked/tombstoned objects.
Backend loss cannot rebuild an equivalent projection from encrypted canonical graph records and checkpoints without consulting model output or remote state.
Graphiti failure cannot use the injected direct-Neo4j fallback while preserving identical typed contracts, provenance, scope, admission, and temporal semantics.

The package would implement learned ontology changes, entity-resolution inference beyond explicit canonical bindings, improve workers, embeddings, community summaries, Memory Router, MCP/API routes, Portainer/Docker packaging, or production rollout.
Canonical graph records would expose plaintext sensitive content, physical vault paths, secrets, or unencrypted claim text.
Any deterministic test requires network access, Graphiti, Neo4j, Hindsight, Ollama, credentials, containers, or a real user vault.
A required change falls outside allowed_files.
The same verification failure remains unresolved after two attempts.

evidence.findings: `entries.jsonl.aead`, `checkpoints.jsonl.aead`, and `tombstones.jsonl.aead` use independently sealed frames containing journal name, working-set ID, monotonic sequence, previous-frame hash, and AEAD bound to that chain position. Appends fsync and reopen the journal before returning.

`manifest.json.aead` contains only a replayed manifest snapshot and journal tail anchors. Missing or corrupt manifests do not lose pins or tombstones; acknowledged journal truncation and frame corruption fail closed.

Pin changes are checkpoint mutations and tombstones have their own authoritative journal. Tombstone is appended and fsynced before canonical episode projection. Tests inject crashes immediately after pin and tombstone frames, then prove pins persist and evidence cannot reopen; rebuild reconciles episode status without resurrection.

Every state read and evidence mutation requires workspace, project, session, and working-set scope; evidence and episode reads additionally bind their IDs. Foreign workspace/project/session calls return unknown errors. Rebuild validates each durable canonical capture envelope and payload hash against the requested scope before accepting it.

Replay initializes every non-tombstoned journal entry as eligible, reapplies final pin/tombstone mutations, and reruns deterministic selection. Tests prove incremental, replayed, and rebuilt selection equality after eviction, late ordering, pin, and unpin operations.

Working-set, evidence, and episode IDs are persisted prefixed UUIDv7 values. Resume scans journal creation records rather than recomputing IDs; duplicate events retain evidence identity. Fork creation validates the parent’s project/workspace and declared parent session, and explicit sibling fork identities produce distinct sets.

The monolithic T004 `state.json.aead` format is neither interpreted nor silently migrated. Discovery explicitly raises `working_interim_format_unsupported`; direct reads expose it only as an unknown invalid working-set ID.

Canonical capture commits first. Working acknowledgement becomes durable only after evidence journal, canonical encrypted episode, checkpoint, manifest snapshot, scoped payload reopening, episode reopening, and hash checks. Failures return degraded non-durable Working metadata while retaining canonical capture. Offload rejects every unsafe/unselected state and always reports replacement and suppression disabled.

Working journals, manifest, and canonical episodes use AEAD and private filesystem permissions. Tests verify payload plaintext does not appear in Working artifacts. Working projections reference the encrypted capture payload rather than duplicating it.

Fresh focused run passes 45/45 tests, including adversarial durability and scope cases. Fresh `npm run verify:codex` and `git diff --check` pass. T014 additionally reports `npm run verify:secrets`, full `npm test`, `npm run verify`, and `npm run verify:release` passing.

PM supplied a fresh full `SuperMemory` index with 8,132 nodes, 13,156 edges, skipped_count=0, persistence=false. Exact findings were verified in checked-out source; deploy remains excluded and is deferred.

T014 changed only approved files and reported no deviations or blockers. The repository remains heavily dirty with user-owned untracked work; this Judge performed no source, state, index, staging, installation, or configuration mutation.
